headline: Bill placed to abolish RAB and form its replacement, the SRB
summary: The Special Response Battalion (SRB) will replace the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) as a specialized unit under the police force with increased accountability.
details: A bill was placed in the Jatiya Sangsad to abolish the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and establish the Special Response Battalion (SRB) as its replacement.
The SRB will function as a specialized unit under the police force, staffed by police officers and members of disciplined forces.
All manpower, assets, funds, and records of RAB will be transferred to the SRB, which will have its own flag, emblem, and uniform.
The SRB will be empowered to investigate criminal offences, conduct searches, arrests, and seizures, and maintain its own lock-up and interrogation facilities.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that the new unit is necessary for a modern, professional, and accountable unit to ensure public security and suppress organized crime.
Opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam and Opposition Leader Shafiqur Rahman opposed the move, demanding detailed parliamentary discussion before forming a new elite force.
Nahid Islam described RAB as a 'symbol of fascism' and noted that political parties had promised to abolish it before elections.
The bill has been sent to the Parliamentary Standing Committee on the Ministry of Home Affairs for scrutiny, with a report due within four working days.
Additionally, the Armed Police Battalion (APBn) Bill 2026 was also introduced to operate the APBn under the police force with authority to investigate criminal offences.
caption:
RAB is being abolished. A new elite force, the Special Response Battalion (SRB), is set to take its place.

A bill was placed in the Jatiya Sangsad to abolish the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and establish the Special Response Battalion (SRB) as its replacement.

The SRB will function as a specialized unit under the police force, staffed by police officers and members of disciplined forces.

All manpower, assets, funds, and records of RAB will be transferred to the SRB, which will have its own flag, emblem, and uniform.

The SRB will be empowered to investigate criminal offences, conduct searches, arrests, and seizures, and maintain its own lock-up and interrogation facilities.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that the new unit is necessary for a modern, professional, and accountable unit to ensure public security and suppress organized crime.

Opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam and Opposition Leader Shafiqur Rahman opposed the move, demanding detailed parliamentary discussion before forming a new elite force.

Nahid Islam described RAB as a 'symbol of fascism' and noted that political parties had promised to abolish it before elections.

The bill has been sent to the Parliamentary Standing Committee on the Ministry of Home Affairs for scrutiny, with a report due within four working days.

Additionally, the Armed Police Battalion (APBn) Bill 2026 was also introduced to operate the APBn under the police force with authority to investigate criminal offences.

headline: Woman killed by state minister's car in Bogura
summary: A pedestrian woman was killed after being hit by the official SUV of State Minister Abdul Bari, who was also injured in the accident.
details: A woman named Firoza was killed after being hit by the official SUV of State Minister Abdul Bari in Bogura.
The accident occurred when the vehicle collided with the pedestrian, sending the car off the road and into a nearby field.
State Minister Abdul Bari and his wife were both injured in the collision.
According to reports, Firoza was on her way to her daughter's house when the accident happened.
Following the incident, State Minister Abdul Bari was transported to Dhaka for advanced medical treatment.
The collision involved a government-issued SUV, and local authorities are investigating the situation.
